clue.text: Clay boxes people left behind, sold initially for pound

indicators.note: one thing standing for another means a letter in the word is swapped out
initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: laggards are those who fall behind the rest
the opening letter of sold
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Clay boxes are abandoned by people and sold off cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of LAGGARDS (pound) gives way to S, leaving SAGGARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saggards (saggars) are fireclay cases in which pottery is fired in a kiln.

clue.text: Puny little son needs to eat greedily

blocks.note: S is the short form of son
to cram is to stuff food down

explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a dialect adjective meaning withered or stunted, hence feeble.

clue.text: Grim canoeist flexing muscles

blocks.note: all twelve letters used as fodder

explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, a canoeist paddling would flex muscles, though the calf ones are less used than the arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The gastrocnemius is the main calf muscle; the plural takes the Latin -ii ending.

clue.text: Lass not available for one, making one scowl

the Roman numeral for one

clue.text: Drug making one leaner somehow with unknown content

clue.text: Be off-putting — as cricketers will ultimately, to get advantage?

explanation.definitionFit: Sledging means distracting an opponent with insults, which is being deliberately off-putting.

clue.text: Man in cave is smart, not revealing name

explanation.definitionFit: Stag is old slang for one who watches or spies, the sentry who cries cave.

clue.text: Off-road driver straggles over island

the Isle of Man
